title: Do 97% of Day Traders Really Lose Money?

generation.notes: Revised against the rebuilt package: needsEvidence cleared. The Brazil population and period (chague L30-L36, L394-L404) and the Taiwan population, period and share unprofitable (barber-odean L39-L46) are now cited on most-retail-day-traders-lose-money.

sentences.text: On YouTube, Riley Coleman films himself growing a tiny futures account, and says the point is "showing you what's possible if you follow a disciplined, consistent strategy".

assertions.text: Riley Coleman's video on growing a small futures account says it is about "showing you what's possible if you follow a disciplined, consistent strategy".

quote.text: showing you what's possible if you follow a disciplined, consistent strategy
quote.speaker: Riley Coleman

sentences.note: The video title says Trading Futures and the context says he starts small; no account figure is read.

sentences.text: If discipline is what it takes, how many of the people who try actually end up ahead?
Researchers in Brazil and Taiwan counted, and they counted the winners too.
sentences.note: Names the two documents the investigation uses (Brazil day-trader study, Taiwan day-trader study); both report their profitable minority.

sentences.text: Ross Cameron of Warrior Trading tells beginners to "learn a strategy that is proven profitable by someone else even if there's no guarantee it'll work for you".

assertions.text: Ross Cameron tells beginners to "learn a strategy that is proven profitable by someone else even if there's no guarantee it'll work for you".

quote.text: learn a strategy that is proven profitable by someone else even if there's no guarantee it'll work for you
quote.speaker: Ross Cameron

sentences.text: Another channel, RP Profits, is blunter: "The strategy is real. The math is real, and there's people using it right now to make money."

assertions.text: RP Profits says "The strategy is real. The math is real, and there's people using it right now to make money."

quote.text: The strategy is real. The math is real, and there's people using it right now to make money.
quote.speaker: RP Profits

sentences.text: Yet the Warrior Trading blog itself carries the line "Trading is risky, and most day traders lose money."

assertions.text: The Warrior Trading blog says "Trading is risky, and most day traders lose money."

quote.text: Trading is risky, and most day traders lose money.
quote.speaker: Warrior Trading

sentences.text: The Brazilian study followed people who began day trading in the country's equity futures market between 2013 and 2015, and sorted them by how many days they kept at it.

assertions.text: The Brazil study observes individuals who began to day trade between 2013 and 2015 in the Brazilian equity futures market.
qualifications: Names the market (equity futures, not stocks) and the period, so every Brazil figure after it carries them.
The ESMA CFD figures qualify this claim for a different product; the sentence asserts only the cited study's population and finding and says nothing about CFDs.

assertions.text: The Brazil day-trader study computed the net profit of each new day trader, grouped by the number of days they day traded.
qualifications: Reports the grouping only; the study does not test setup quality.

sentences.text: Of those who tried it for a single day, 29.8 percent made a net profit, and the share fell at every step after that.

assertions.text: In the Brazil study, 29.8% of those who day traded for one day obtained a positive net profit, and the proportion of successful day traders decreases monotonically with the number of days traded.
qualifications: s10 says this is a pattern in who profited, compared to roulette; the study does not test setup quality or why.

sentences.text: The authors compare it to roulette, where the more rounds people play, the fewer come out ahead.

assertions.text: The Brazil study's authors liken the falling proportion of successful day traders to casino roulette, where the proportion of successful players decreases with the number of rounds played.
qualifications: The sentence reports the authors' comparison only; it says nothing about setup quality or fatigue, which the study does not measure.

sentences.text: Of the 1,551 who kept going for more than 300 days, 97 percent lost money after fees, and only 47 came out ahead.

assertions.text: In the Brazil study, 97% of the 1,551 individuals who day traded for more than 300 days lost money net of exchange and brokerage fees.
qualifications: Population is the persistent traders in Brazilian equity futures, 2013-2015, named in s08.
The ESMA CFD figures qualify this claim for a different product; the sentence asserts only the cited study's population and finding and says nothing about CFDs.

assertions.text: Only 47 of the 1,551 persistent day traders in the Brazil study profited net of fees.
qualifications: States the narrower finding: a small minority of persistent traders profited.

sentences.text: Only 17 earned more than Brazil's minimum wage, and the single best averaged 310 dollars a day.

assertions.text: Only 17 of the 1,551 earned more than the Brazilian minimum wage, and the individual who earned the most earned US$310 per day on average.
qualifications: Earnings are the study's average daily profit; s13 says even the top earners' results swung widely.

sentences.text: And the handful who beat a bank teller's starting pay got there on a roller coaster, their daily results swinging by hundreds to thousands of dollars.

assertions.text: The individuals in the Brazil study who earned more than a bank teller's initial salary did so with great volatility; the standard deviation of their daily profit ranged from US$632 to US$3,308.
qualifications: Speaks of the standard deviation in words; it is of daily profit for the top earners only.

sentences.note: 'Hundreds to thousands' paraphrases the standard deviation range 632 to 3,308; 'handful' is the eight the passage names.

sentences.text: Did the ones who stayed at least get better with practice?
The study found no evidence that they learned.

assertions.text: The Brazil study finds no evidence of learning among persistent day traders.
qualifications: Attributed to the Brazil study only; s19 gives Taiwan's different finding on past winners.

sentences.text: A second study, of individual investors who day traded in Taiwan from 1992 to 2006, found the vast majority of them unprofitable.

assertions.text: In the Taiwan study of individual investors who day traded from 1992 to 2006, the vast majority of day traders are unprofitable.
qualifications: Names the population and period; a different market and era from Brazil, which s28 says for the whole answer.
The ESMA CFD figures qualify this claim for a different product; the sentence asserts only the cited study's population and finding and says nothing about CFDs.

sentences.text: Taken as a group, they lost 7 basis points a day before costs, where a basis point is a hundredth of a percent, and trading costs more than tripled that loss, to 23.9.

assertions.text: In the Taiwan study, day traders lose 7 basis points a day on average before costs, and trading costs more than triple the losses to 23.9 basis points per day.
qualifications: 'Taken as a group' carries that this is an aggregate return, not the share of traders who lost (s27 gives that).

sentences.text: So is anyone reliably good at this?
A few are: in Taiwan, traders who had already been profitable, with more than 40 days of day trading in the past year, went on to earn more than their trading costs.

assertions.text: In the Taiwan study, profitable traders with more than 40 days of day trading experience in the last year earn more than enough to cover their transaction costs.
qualifications: s19 says these predictably profitable traders were under 3% of day traders.

sentences.text: But those predictably profitable traders made up less than 3 percent of all day traders on an average day.

assertions.text: In the Taiwan study, predictably profitable traders constitute less than 3% of all day traders on an average day.
qualifications: States the narrower finding: a small predictably profitable minority, not that a strategy makes traders consistent.

sentences.text: Ross Cameron names one reason the rest struggle: "when you trade against the high frequency trading algorithms, trading large caps, you really don't have a good edge".

assertions.text: Ross Cameron says "when you trade against the high frequency trading algorithms, trading large caps, you really don't have a good edge".

quote.text: when you trade against the high frequency trading algorithms, trading large caps, you really don't have a good edge
quote.speaker: Ross Cameron

sentences.text: The Brazilian futures data point the same way in a different market: when high-frequency traders' share of deals rose by 10 percent, individuals' average loss was 19 percent higher.

assertions.text: In the Brazil study, individuals' average loss is 19% higher when the fraction of deals by high-frequency traders increases by 10%.
qualifications: 'Futures' and 'a different market' carry that this was not large-cap stocks; 'when ... was higher' reports a link, not a measured cause.

sentences.text: So yes: in both studies most people lost, and in Brazil the longer they kept at it, the worse their odds of being ahead.

assertions.text: In the Brazil study 97% of those who day traded more than 300 days lost money net of fees, and the share with a positive net profit fell with the number of days traded.
qualifications: Points back to s09-s11 in words; s28 limits the answer to these markets and years.

assertions.text: In the Taiwan study the vast majority of day traders are unprofitable.
qualifications: Points back to s27 in words.
The ESMA CFD figures qualify this claim for a different product; the sentence asserts only the cited study's population and finding and says nothing about CFDs.

sentences.text: Some people do beat the odds, and in Taiwan the ones who had been winning tended to keep winning, but they were a sliver of everyone who tried.

assertions.text: In the Taiwan study an extensive history of profitability is a strong predictor of future profitability, but very few traders are predictably profitable.
qualifications: Points back to s18-s19 in words: a small predictably profitable minority.

sentences.text: Both studies looked at other markets and other years than today's American stock market, so they give the odds there, not a law for every market.
sentences.note: The limit that applies to the whole answer: Brazilian equity futures 2013-2015 and Taiwan 1992-2006 (s08, s27); no US momentum-stock traders are measured.

sentences.text: What these counts can't do is check any one trader's month: a screenshot of a small account turned into a big one is neither confirmed nor ruled out by a tally of everyone who tried.
sentences.note: States what the evidence cannot answer (brief: say it cannot). Neither study measures any individual's best month or any seller's record.

sentences.text: If someone sells you a strategy as consistent, ask for audited results across every account and every month, not the best screenshot.
And if you try it anyway, put in only what you can afford to lose, and judge yourself by your results after fees, not by your best day.
